lanes.title: battle outcomes: fighting means damage, a tie is a tie, the Standoff tie, one role per side, the ambush on the map, 'fought' required, the player's capture choice, the two test battles inside the thirds (D-087, D-088, D-089 DH1-DH2, D-090 DI1)
lanes.brief:
SCOPE LIMITS: work only in prototypes/m7-sprint1 (M7Proto.slnx; M7Econ.slnx only if economy code is touched) and docs/m7-plan; no change to Sim.Core, Sim.Data, Sim.Cli, Sim.Ui or their tests, no permanent project, no CI change (D-079 §6, Q5 open). Design is marked PROPOSAL where the Director delegated it; every reading is labelled READING with both alternatives; no Director decision is invented or reopened. Terms (D-088 DG11): the BATTLEFIELD is the small area where a battle is fought; the MAP is the world map; use the two words exactly in code comments, documents and reports.

READ FIRST, in full: docs/d087-ties-battalions-autoresolve-director-answers-2026-11-12.md, docs/d088-battalion-limits-healing-walls-director-answers-2026-11-12.md, docs/d089-fought-capture-choice-research-tree-launcher-director-answers-2026-11-12.md and docs/d090-test-battles-dr24-battalions-export-director-answers-2026-11-12.md (decisions, readings, what each supersedes or narrows); then D-082 (DA1, DA6, DA7), D-083 (DB1) and D-085 (DD1) as narrowed; D-079 DR29, DR31 and DIR5 §2.14 (the deployment thirds); docs/m7-plan/morale-proposal.md (§11, §12, the rally rules), docs/m7-plan/concealment-actions-proposal.md and docs/m7-plan/notification-panel-proposal.md (N-301); reports H-MOR3, H-AP, H-TR (P-TR1, P-TR13), H-P (battery P, and why the Sprint 1 ambush is excluded), H-N (Amphibious), H-S (the immediate assault), H-W (dispositions and their refusals), H-U (U-F4, U-Q11, U2-5).

(1) FIGHTING IS DAMAGE (D-087 DF7; DF7-R1 (a) and DF7-R2 (a), confirmed by D-088 DG7; it replaces D-085 DD1-R2 (a)). Both resolvers report fighting as the first instant at which any strength (hit points or persons, as each resolver counts it) is lost to an enemy attack, in every domain (melee, missiles, crew-served and domain weapons, boarding, ramming): lane MOR3's report of the first attack resolved (BattleResult.FirstFightMs and Fought) becomes the first damage. Re-state READINGS MOR3-R1 and MOR3-R2 under damage (what changes, what becomes moot). The settlement: if damage was dealt in the battle it settles as before (D-083's entry cost, DR29's decrease, DA1's rise for a winner; D-083 DB1 is narrowed to such battles); if no damage was dealt at all, no army's morale changes; the row records it (bump the codec version if the row changes). The in-battle entry part (PROPOSAL C1, default 0) is charged at the first damage instant. MEASURE on lane P's battery and in the War Sandbox how many battles had attacks but no damage, and report the change.

(2) 'FOUGHT' IS A REQUIRED INPUT (D-089 DH1). SupportBattle.Fought (today defaulting to true) becomes required at the battle hand-off: a missing value is refused with a stable refusal code, never read as 'yes'. Every caller and test states it; tests for the refusal and for both values.

(3) A TIE IS A TIE (D-087 DF8 and DF11; this supersedes D-082 DA6 and, since an equal ambush is a tie too, DA7-R's ambusher win). In both resolvers, through the one shared function (EqualSides.Decide), equal sides report no winner, ambush or not; keep the WinBasis codes stable (a basis no longer produced stays reserved and documented). Both armies come out with what is left. At the end of a tie, routing units turn back into normal units with decreased morale and rejoin their armies (DF8-R1 (a), DG7); after a win or a loss the morale proposal's rally rules stand. The size of the decrease is a value in the morale proposal: PROPOSE a default with its reasoning (a TUNE value). A tie raises no morale (D-082 DA1 unchanged). Tests in both resolvers, including an equal ambush.

(4) THE STANDOFF TIE (D-087 DF10; lane TR's P-TR1 is ratified). A Standoff (nobody progresses, both sides holding) ends the battle in a tie in both resolvers. Retire the DA6-R extension flag (TacticalRules.EqualSidesAtStandoff) or fix it on, and say which and why. Tests.

(5) ROLES (D-087 DF8's rule; D-088 DG8: one role per side, which replaces DF8-R2 (a)). A side is the attacker or the defender, and every army on a side shares the side's role; a side holds one empire's armies, or an empire's and its allies'. The attacker is the side that initiates combat; declaring war, a zone of control or a siege without combat does not make a side the attacker. Battles built from an engagement (EngagementBattle, the War Sandbox) take their roles from the engagement that opened the battle, never from a war declaration. For the ambush battle of item 6: READING OC-R1 (a) the ambushing side initiates combat, so it is the attacker; (b) the passing side is the attacker, since its move triggered the battle. Apply (a) and label it. Tests, including armies of two empires and their allies on one side.

(6) THE AMBUSH ON THE MAP (D-087 DF9; D-088 DG9 and DG10; DG10 replaces DF9-R2 (a)). An ambush happens when an enemy unit's move on the map passes through the region of a unit that is hidden there and undetected by every enemy. The region's radius is about 10 km, plus or minus 10 km by the HIDDEN army's size (DG9): a larger army watches up to about 20 km, a smaller one down toward 0; the curve is a TUNE value (PROPOSAL, with its reasoning). Check the whole path, not only its end point (the distance from the hidden unit to each segment of the move, in exact integer arithmetic, never float), at the instant of passage. When several hidden units or several movers qualify at one instant, order them by a composite key with a stable integer tie-break and prove it with a tie-dense test. The battle then starts by itself (no order is needed), the ambusher is revealed (its concealment ends, and that is recorded), and the battlefield is built with every side in its own third (DR31 holds: DeploymentRule.Thirds, with the deployment check passing). The ambusher's advantage comes from the terrain, from the concealment it carries into the battle (lane N's personal concealment, lane AP's camouflage factor) and from its posture, never from an illegal start. State the map unit the war layer uses and its conversion to km, citing the code. Pins: a turn-exact pin for when the battle starts relative to the move that triggered it, and a live-versus-replay pin. Reconcile lane AP's attack-from-concealment path with DF9 (keep, adapt or retire it, with the reason) and amend concealment-actions-proposal.md in place with dated notes.

(7) THE PLAYER'S CAPTURE CHOICE (D-089 DH2, answering lane U's U-Q11; DH2-R1). When the player's own immediate assault (lane S's immediate assault order) takes a city, the player is asked 'Occupy, sack or raze?' at the moment of capture: the capture raises a decision instant then, after the order's consequences, so the choice is offered and does not lapse (U-F4, U2-5). An AI taker still disposes by its doctrine at the moment of capture (unchanged). Lane W's refusals are unchanged (no sack or raze of one's own population; never the last city). Turn-exact pins for both paths; amend N-301 in notification-panel-proposal.md in place (dated).

(8) THE TWO TEST BATTLES (D-090 DI1). Rewrite ParityScenarios' Sprint 1 'ambush' (ParityScenarioId.Ambush: its ambushers stand in the middle third, H-TR P-TR13) and lane N's MultiDomainScenarios.Amphibious (its four defending shore formations, 20-23, stand in the middle third) so that every side deploys in its own third (DeploymentRule.Thirds, with the check passing). The ambush comes from a jungle or forest belt that the advancing side must cross from its own third; the landing comes from a force approaching from the sea to a shore that its defender holds inside its own third. Each scenario keeps its stated purpose. Every pin they hold moves with a measured attribution (old value, new value, cause): among them VerificationRound1TRTests (its refusal pin becomes an acceptance pin), DomainOrdersAndGoldenTests, NavalTests, TerrainDomainInterplayTests, EqualSidesTests, AutoResolverTests and AutoResolverPTests. State in the report that the rewritten Ambush is deployment-legal, for lane AR's battery.

(9) DOCUMENTS AND CHECKS. morale-proposal.md and concealment-actions-proposal.md gain sections for items 1-6 (PROPOSAL where design), with superseded statements struck in place under dated bold notes ([OC, date, D-08x ...]). A semantic test per mechanism, in both resolvers wherever a rule is in both; a populated-table round-trip test for every new or changed serialized row (exact ExpectedLength, bit-exact round-trip, hash equality); lane P's battery re-measured where outputs change, and identity digests where they must not change; bounded mutants with semantic kills; the determinism scan; the doc-link check.
